title: Introducing OlmoEarth Embeddings: Custom Embedding Exports for Earth Observation Analysis
summary: OlmoEarth Studio, a platform for building Earth observation models, now allows users to compute and export embedding vectors—compact numerical representations of Earth-observation data generated by open-source OlmoEarth foundation models. These embeddings enable various downstream tasks such as similarity search, few-shot segmentation, change detection, and unsupervised exploration. Users can customize embeddings by selecting areas of interest, time ranges, encoder variants, resolutions, and imagery sources. The exported Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) are lightweight and compatible with geospatial tools like QGIS and GDAL. The article provides practical examples and code snippets for leveraging these embeddings in real-world applications.
key_points: OlmoEarth Studio enables the computation and export of embedding vectors from Earth-observation data using open-source foundation models.
Embeddings are compact numerical representations that support tasks like similarity search, segmentation, and change detection without requiring extensive labeled data.
Users can customize embeddings via parameters such as area of interest, time span, encoder variant (Nano, Tiny, Base), spatial resolution, and imagery sources (Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1).
Exported embeddings are stored as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) with int8 values, which can be dequantized to floating-point vectors for analysis.

Practical applications include similarity search (finding locations with similar surface characteristics), few-shot segmentation (land-cover mapping with minimal labels), change detection (identifying surface changes over time), and unsupervised exploration (visualizing landscape structure using PCA).
The embeddings are highly performant, as demonstrated by benchmarks and independent evaluations, and can be fine-tuned for higher performance using supervised fine-tuning (SFT).
Code examples and tutorials are provided for integrating embeddings into workflows using tools like Python, rasterio, and scikit-learn.
Limitations include potential variability in embedding quality due to input imagery quality (e.g., cloud cover, atmospheric artifacts).
